description.value: Participants recalled negative autobiographical memories and used feel, accept, or analyze strategies, followed by ratings and an arrow direction task.

spans.text: Participants viewed three repetitions each of three types of stimulus blocks (feel, accept, or analyze) whose order was counterbalanced.

description.value: Participants recalled the cued negative autobiographical memory and focused for 30 seconds on the specific feelings that naturally flowed through their mind, a strategy designed to facilitate negative-affect-infused rumination.

spans.text: The first “feel” strategy directed individuals to focus on the specific feelings that naturally flowed through their mind as they thought about their recalled experiences.
accept
strategy cue word appeared on screen directing them to engage in the feel, accept, or analyze strategy

description.value: Participants recalled the cued negative autobiographical memory and for 30 seconds recognized their experienced feelings as passing mental events psychologically distant from the self and not controlling them, a strategy designed to undermine rumination.

spans.text: The second “accept” strategy directed individuals to recognize that the feelings they experienced during recollection were passing mental events that were psychologically distant from the self and did not control them.
analyze
strategy cue word appeared on screen directing them to engage in the feel, accept, or analyze strategy

description.value: Participants recalled the cued negative autobiographical memory and for 30 seconds objectively analyzed the causes and reasons underlying their feelings, a memory analogue of cognitive reappraisal.

spans.text: The third “analyze” strategy directed participants to objectively analyze the causes and reasons underlying their feelings
Finally, participants engaged in a 30-second spatial perception task in which they saw an arrow pointing left or right and were asked to indicate which direction the arrow was pointing.
baseline condition

description.value: For 30 seconds, participants viewed arrows pointing left or right and indicated the direction of each arrow. This active baseline was intended not to engage the regulatory, memory, and emotional processes of interest.

spans.text: Finally, participants engaged in a 30-second spatial perception task in which they saw an arrow pointing left or right and were asked to indicate which direction the arrow was pointing.
Each block was comprised of three 80-second trials.

stimuli.value: cue phrases and strategy cue words; arrows pointing left or right

instructions.value: Participants recalled highly arousing negative autobiographical memories in response to cue phrases and then implemented one of three strategies for 30 seconds: feel, focusing on the specific feelings that naturally arose; accept, recognizing the feelings as passing mental events psychologically distant from and not controlling the self; or analyze, objectively examining the causes and reasons underlying the feelings. They then rated arousal and negativity and completed a spatial arrow-direction task.
